findings.title: Changed ordinary Claude results are silently replaced before final idle
findings.evidence: RunState stores every accepted ordinary success result by assignment. If state is running or a background task is outstanding, complete() is false, allowing a second current-session ordinary result with a new UUID to overwrite the first. The Core calls claude_terminal only once, on the last result after idle; Collector therefore emits Complete for the replacement without seeing contradictory content. This contradicts native-result design 2.2 (changed/multiple ordinary final representations are ambiguous).
findings.legitimate_trigger: Owned Claude init, session state running, ordinary success text A, distinct-UUID ordinary success text B, then idle. No foreign Session or forged receipt is needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Track qualified ordinary candidate identity/content as each result is accepted, and preserve sticky ambiguity; do not rely on the final RunState.result slot as the complete acquisition history. Keep background/origin/final-idle qualification.
findings.causal_control_not_executed: Actual stdio fixture emits A then B while completion is held by running state; after idle require Ambiguous/no complete text. Identical redelivery should remain idempotent; foreign-origin content should not poison the owned candidate.

findings.title: Collector overflow never stops the native input loop
findings.evidence: Collector event/item limits only poison status and return (). Core codex loop does not inspect this status or receive a bounded-stop indication. After 1024 relevant events or 256 item IDs it continues reading arbitrary further frames until a terminal or external cancellation, retaining the native lease. The approved supplement 3 explicitly requires stopping collection/invocation at overflow rather than reading an unbounded suffix. Per-frame JSON bounds do not bound total events or elapsed resource ownership.
findings.legitimate_trigger: The exact owned thread/turn emits 1025 bounded agentMessage delta notifications and continues emitting without turn/completed.
findings.suggested_fix: Return a sticky bounded acquisition overflow signal to the actor, stop reading and invoke existing owned best-effort shutdown. Preserve an already observed native terminal separately; otherwise work remains Unknown and acquisition Overflow.
findings.causal_control_not_executed: Owned fixture emits the overflow boundary and then waits without terminal. Require bounded terminal/receipt Overflow and no continued model-frame drain; omission of actor overflow handling must reach and fail that assertion.

findings.title: Pre-wire input admission validates the old immutable Context but not the current Task pointer
findings.evidence: register_native_session initially compares Task.context_version to input.version. Later reserve_native_input only reloads invocation.context_version and checks that old immutable row hash is unchanged. validate_authority checks lifecycle/governing Project/Goal and executor namespace, but not the Task Context pointer. A legitimate standalone Task can append Context 2 and update its pointer after registration while native bootstrap is awaiting. Context 1 remains immutable, so the old input is admitted and may later receive OwnedTerminal despite having been superseded before its first input. This is current grant/receipt currency, not missing future Runtime integration.
findings.legitimate_trigger: Use the supported standalone current Context fixture, hold Codex thread/start (or Claude initialization) after Session registration, append Context 2 via put_context and update Task.context_version with put_task, then release bootstrap. No Workflow row is required and ordinary Store paths allow the change.
findings.suggested_fix: In the native-input Immediate transaction compare current Task pointer (and the managed current input authority where present) to the private invocation binding, including explicit no-Context identity. Refuse before native_input intent/wire on supersession. Keep already admitted immutable input distinct from later publication.
findings.causal_control_not_executed: Actual bootstrap barrier plus public Context/Task update; assert no native_input effect/wire occurs and no current OwnedTerminal is minted. An unchanged-pointer control must dispatch normally. Test both Some-to-newer and None-to-Some where allowed.

findings.title: Receipt persistence failure discards a known native terminal before retry or historical retention
findings.evidence: After a reliable native Success/Failure, run builds NativeTerminal only inside a temporary closure. Any receipt transaction error drops that proof and proceeds to cleanup/end. Core does not retain the known work/disposition/failure. Drop then retires the open Unit and calls capture with Unknown/Lost after protocol_lost(), even though the terminal was observed. A transient first insert failure can consequently yield a historical Unknown/Partial receipt and lose the observed known work. Supplement 5 requires preserving bounded acquisition/known work on persistence failure and forbids turning known Success into Unknown merely because persistence/hygiene fails.
findings.legitimate_trigger: A genuine native final+terminal is observed, and an isolated test SQL trigger aborts only the first native_results insert (or another recoverable transaction conflict occurs), allowing the subsequent retirement/history path.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the exact private terminal observation/proof in the supervisor across persistence failure; bounded exact retry or historical-only retention must preserve observed work independently of logical Unit retirement. No watch authority may precede commit. Drop-before-native-terminal remains Unknown.
findings.causal_control_not_executed: Inject one receipt insert failure after a real terminal, then permit subsequent writes; require historical observation retains Success/Failure with unchanged content evidence while logical retirement remains conservative, and no watch success appears before receipt commit.
